newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Electricidad de Caracas draws down $166mln capital.
newsitem.headline: Electricidad de Caracas draws down $166mln capital.

text.p: Venezuelan electric company Electricidad de Caracas has had to draw down 78 billion bolivars ($166 million) from its net reserves and capital to cover losses following tariff hike delays in 1996, the company said.
"But we're hopeful -- and there's even room to be optimistic -- that next year the government will implement its new tariff scheme," a company spokesman told Reuters.
In contrast to the current tariff-setting system, the government has said it will establish a transparent and more automatic adjustment mechanism in January.

So far this year the government had granted Electricidad tariff increases totalling 74.58 percent while required increases to cover exchange rate and inflation losses are 142.60 percent, company Vice President for Sales Inaki Rousse told the Congressional Services Commission Wednesday.
Electricidad recently reported an inflation-adjusted nine month profit of 42 billion bolivars vs 57 billion over the same period in the year before.
